correctness.rationale: The affine reproducing kernel follows from polygon rotational covariance, convexity places the maximum at vertices, kernel symmetry equates L1/L∞ norms, and polygon clipping yields exact cap moments. A uniform angular-cell cancellation lemma suppresses inverse-square measure errors against piecewise C2 angular absolute-kernel functions when compared to a radius 1-pi²/(3n²) disk; expanding its kernel then yields the displayed coefficient and O(fourth-order) remainder. Exact triangle/square/hexagon values and independent polar quadrature provide finite checks only.

Even an exactly known disk value supplies only the leading term, not the explicit finite-polygon caps or the positive inverse-square defect.

value.rationale: The L∞ Lebesgue norm of a least-squares projector is a natural sharp uniform error amplification constant. The theorem gives exact geometric finite data for all regular polygon side counts, plus a nonzero sharp second-order stability loss toward a disk with a structural fourth-order angular cancellation lemma. This quantifies a meaningful natural domain-discretization boundary, not a gratuitous isolated invariant.
